final_message:
I've calibrated all seven joint offsets and written them to `params.json`. The simulated arm now matches all 12 training photos (4 poses × 3 cameras) down to what looks like the photos' own sensor noise.

| param | value (rad) |
|---|---|
| offset_1 | 0.1437 |
| offset_2 | −0.1768 |
| offset_3 | 0.2231 |
| offset_4 | 0.1572 |
| offset_5 | −0.2419 |
| offset_6 | 0.2045 |
| offset_7 | −0.2965 |

**Method:** The task is purely kinematic (the pose doesn't change over time), so each guess only needs forward kinematics and a render. My score was the mean absolute pixel difference between the renders and the 12 photos. The photos were first blurred slightly to smooth the score out, and the blur was removed at the end.
1. A coarse grid search on each joint in turn, over the full ±0.4 range.
2. A local refinement (Nelder–Mead) at progressively less blur. This moved offset_1 and offset_3 a lot: 0.34 → 0.14 and 0.05 → 0.22. Joints 1 and 3 rotate about nearly the same axis when joint 2 is near zero, which is why the joint-by-joint search couldn't separate them.

**Checks:**
- Moving each offset ±0.03 on its own gives a sharp, symmetric V-shaped rise in error, with the lowest point at the fitted value. Joints 1–4 are pinned down tightly. Joints 5–7 have shallower curves, but their minima are still clearly centered.
- The remaining error is 1.85 / 1.56 / 1.97 (front / side / top) and is almost identical for every pose. That matches the stated sensor noise (std 2.5, so about 2.0 expected; black background pixels pull it lower). There's no pose-dependent error left, which suggests the offsets are real rather than fitted to one pose.
- In a side-by-side of pose_3 (simulation, photo, difference), the difference image was essentially blank.

I only checked against the training poses. The held-out poses can't be tested here.
